extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, businesses, organisations and stakeholders interested in Singapore's climate and decarbonisation policy
extracted.subtask_description: A government consultation inviting views on Singapore’s decarbonisation journey, including climate ambition, transition to a low-carbon economy, and specific decarbonisation measures to inform the next Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Net zero by 2050 (national climate commitment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Singapore's goal to achieve net zero emissions by 2050; public support for this goal and calls to accelerate and set more ambitious targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 91% of respondents were supportive of net zero by 2050; among supporters, 82% wanted Singapore to further accelerate its transition by setting more ambitious climate targets. Several respondents urged more ambitious targets and faster decarbonisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and interim targets for NDCs
rubrics_metrics.description: Greater transparency in how Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) are determined, including setting interim goals and reporting progress towards net zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents suggested setting interim goals towards net zero, reporting the progress of decarbonisation measures, and being more transparent about NDC determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public understanding and clarity of measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Decarbonisation measures should be communicated clearly so the public understands what each measure entails and how it contributes to decarbonisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each measure, more than 75% of respondents stated they understood what the measure entailed (Figure 15). The consultation recommends clear communication of measures' roles in decarbonisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of carbon tax: design and complementary measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Carbon tax should be designed to incentivise decarbonisation (e.g., raise levels, lower taxable thresholds) while being transparent and paired with other measures to mitigate cost-of-living impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions included increasing the carbon tax level, lowering the taxable emissions threshold, ensuring allowances do not lessen impact, making allowance allocation transparent, and implementing the tax alongside other measures. Revenue should be channelled back to citizens, particularly lower-income households.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation and transparency of allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocation of allowances (if any) must be transparent and should not lessen the effectiveness of carbon pricing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents asked that the impact of the carbon tax not be lessened by provision of allowances, and requested more transparency regarding how allowances are allocated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revenue recycling to support vulnerable groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Revenue from carbon pricing should be channelled back to citizens to support lower-income households in managing decarbonisation costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents recommended that carbon tax revenue be returned to citizens, particularly to help low-income households cope with associated costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits and conditions on carbon capture and storage (CCS)
rubrics_metrics.description: CCS should be limited to hard-to-abate sectors, coupled with emission reduction measures, not used to prolong fossil fuel use, and avoid detriment to host countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents wanted CCS restricted to sectors where emissions are hard to abate, coupled with measures to reduce emissions, and cautioned about technological maturity, scalability, and impacts on host storage sites. Some suggested exploring direct air capture and other removal solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carbon credit integrity and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Carbon credits used must be of high integrity, must not harm source countries, and should not be a substitute for companies' own emission reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents called for regulations ensuring high-integrity credits, expanding partner countries for credits, and preventing companies from using credits to 'pay their way out' of decarbonisation; credits should accompany plans to reduce emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imported low‑carbon electricity: source and impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: When importing electricity, ensure it is from fully renewable sources and consider the social, economic and environmental impacts on source countries; avoid over-dependence on imports given cost, security and intermittency concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents stressed that imported electricity should be fully renewable and that projects should consider impacts on source countries; others worried about dependence because of cost, security, and intermittency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximise domestic solar deployment and address lifecycle issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximise domestic solar deployment (including subsidies for private rooftops) while addressing concerns about panel material sourcing and end-of-life treatment/disposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents suggested subsidising rooftop solar and maximising domestic deployment, but raised concerns over material sustainability and disposal at end of life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy demand reduction and efficiency measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Decarbonisation should include demand reduction (incentives to reduce peak consumption), improved energy efficiency, long-duration storage, and reduced cooling demand through temperature settings and building design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideas included incentives for lower peak use, long-duration storage systems, raising temperatures in malls/offices/public transport, effective building design, and reconsidering siting data centres. Explore technologies like nuclear (SMRs), green hydrogen, wind, and hydro as additional options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of natural gas as a transitional fuel
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural gas will remain a key fuel in the near term; policy should improve the energy and carbon efficiency of natural gas generation while scaling up other low-carbon options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural gas currently makes up 95% of Singapore's electricity supply; the government views it as a transitional fuel and aims to improve efficiency of generation units during the transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry transformation and targeted support
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with industries to transform value chains, create sustainable products, pursue carbon abatement (e.g., Sustainable Jurong Island), and provide incentives and grants to support decarbonisation planning, MRV, and transition costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Sustainable Jurong Island plans to increase sustainable product output and carbon abatement targets; respondents asked for more grants covering measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) and broader transition planning support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentives for companies to decarbonise
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide attractive incentives (grants, subsidies) to help companies decarbonise so they can remain competitive; public views vary on sufficiency of current incentives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 44% agreed the Government has provided attractive incentives; some respondents recommended expanding grants and subsidies to accelerate decarbonisation and to keep costs of low-carbon goods lower than higher-carbon alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stronger disincentives for carbon emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Put in place policies that provide companies with stronger disincentives to emit carbon (e.g., higher carbon tax, stricter emissions regulations) to accelerate decarbonisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 77% agreed Singapore should have stronger disincentives; of those, 64% stated they would pay more for goods/services from companies that decarbonise faster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability and anti‑greenwashing for corporations
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold companies accountable for climate targets, prevent greenwashing, and require transparency from firms receiving decarbonisation grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents urged that companies be held accountable to their climate targets to prevent greenwashing; those tapping grants should be transparent about sustainability plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transport sector measures and trade-off considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage walking, cycling and public transport; subsidise EVs and EV infrastructure; regulate internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles and reduce private vehicle numbers while considering electricity demand and material sustainability of EVs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents supported EV subsidies and infrastructure, better public transport and cycling infrastructure, and further regulation of ICE vehicles. Concerns included increased electricity demand before a fully renewable grid and unsustainable materials in EV batteries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waste reduction and recycling
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase recycling rates and reduce waste, particularly reducing reliance on single-use plastics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents called for more efforts to reduce waste and increase recycling to lower dependence on single-use plastics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forestry, agriculture and nature‑based solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid deforestation, explore nature-based climate solutions, promote reduced meat consumption, and make food production more sustainable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents recommended nature-based solutions and dietary shifts (eat less meat) as part of decarbonisation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public education and behavioural nudges
rubrics_metrics.description: Educate the public on climate change and decarbonisation efforts, encourage behavioral change from a young age through schools, and use nudges to shift consumer behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents wanted more education on climate change and suggested behavioural nudges and school programmes to encourage early habit formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design of public consultations and citizen engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Future consultations should include more engagements, more open‑ended questions, and cover topics like nuclear energy and adaptation measures to solicit deeper feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents requested more consultations and engagement, more open-ended questions, and broader topic coverage (e.g., nuclear and adaptation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage trade‑offs and provide social/economic supports
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognise and manage the costs and trade-offs of decarbonisation for companies, workers and households by providing supports, retraining, and policies to protect competitiveness and livelihoods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents noted disruptions to business models and jobs, and recommended green skills programmes, retraining, measures to protect competitiveness, and policies to prevent undue cost-of-living increases.
